title: One sun of righteousness, many anointed
source_text: Διὸ καὶ χρεία οὐκ ἦν πολλὰ γενέσθαι πανταχοῦ σώματα καὶ πολλὰ ἀνάλογον τῷ Ἰησοῦ πνεύματα, ἵν᾿ ἡ πᾶσα τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἰκουμένη φωτισθῇ τῷ λόγῳ τοῦ θεοῦ. ἤρκει γὰρ ὁ εἷς λόγος, ὡς „δικαιοσύνης ἥλιος“ ἀνατείλας, ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἐκπέμψαι τὰς ἐπὶ τὴν ψυχὴν τῶν βουλομένων αὐτὸν παραδέξασθαι φθανούσας αὐγάς. εἰ δὲ καὶ πολλά τις ποθεῖ σώματα πεπληρωμένα θείου πνεύματος ἰδεῖν, ἀνάλογον ἐκείνῳ τῷ ἑνὶ Χριστῷ διακονούμενα τῇ πανταχοῦ τῶν ἀνθρώπων σωτηρίᾳ, κατανοείτω τοὺς πανταχοῦ ὑγιῶς καὶ μετὰ βίου ὀρθοῦ διδάσκοντας τὸν Ἰησοῦ λόγον, Χριστοὺς καὶ αὐτοὺς ὑπὸ τῶν θείων γραφῶν καλουμένους ἐν τῷ „μὴ ἅπτεσθε τῶν Χριστῶν μου, καὶ ἐν τοῖς προφήταις μου μὴ πονηρεύεσθε.“ καὶ γὰρ ὥσπερ ἠκούσαμεν „ὅτι ἀντίχριστος ἔρχεται,“ καὶ οὐδὲν ἧττον μεμαθήκαμεν ὅτι „ἀντίχριστοι πολλοί“ εἰσιν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ· τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον ὅτι Χριστὸς ἐπιδεδήμηκε γνόντες θεωροῦμεν ὅτι δι᾿ αὐτὸν πολλοὶ Χριστοὶ γεγόνασιν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, οἵτινες ἀνάλογον ἐκείνῳ ἠγάπησαν „δικαιοσύνην καὶ“ ἐμίσησαν „ἀδικίαν· καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἔχρισε“ καὶ αὐτοὺς „ὁ θεὸς, ὁ θεὸς“ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, „ἐλαίῳ ἀγαλλιάσεως.“ ἀλλ᾿ ἐκεῖνος μὲν οὖν ὑπὲρ „τοὺς μετόχους“ αὐτοῦ ἀγαπήσας „δικαιοσύνην καὶ“ μισήσας „ἀνομίαν“ καὶ τὴν ἀπαρχὴν εἴληφε τοῦ χρίσματος καὶ, εἰ χρὴ οὕτως ὀνομάσαι, ὅλον τὸ χρῖσμα τοῦ τῆς „ἀγαλλιάσεως“ ἐλαίου· οἱ δὲ μέτοχοι αὐτοῦ, ἕκαστος ὡς κεχώρηκε, μετέσχον καὶ τοῦ χρίσματος αὐτοῦ. διόπερ, ἐπεὶ Χριστὸς „κεφαλή“ ἐστι „τῆς ἐκκλησίας,“ ὡς εἶναι ἓν σῶμα Χριστὸν καὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, τὸ „μύρον ἐπὶ κεφαλῆς“ καταβέβηκεν „ἐπὶ τὸν πώγωνα,“ τὰ σύμβολα τοῦ τελείου ἀνδρὸς „Ἀαρὼν,“ καὶ ἔφθασε „καταβαῖνον“ τοῦτο τὸ „μύρον“ „ἐπὶ τὴν ὤαν τοῦ ἐνδύματος αὐτοῦ.“ καὶ ταῦτα δέ μοι λέλεκται πρὸς τὸν ἄσεμνον τοῦ Κέλσου λόγον εἰπόντος· δέον πολλὰ ὁμοίως διαφυσῆσαι σώματα καὶ κατὰ πᾶσαν ἀποστεῖλαι τὴν οἰκουμένην. ὁ μὲν οὖν κωμῳδὸς γελωτοποιῶν τὸν Δία κοιμώμενον πεποίηκέ τε καὶ διϋπνιζόμενον καὶ πέμποντα πρὸς τοὺςἝλ ληνας τὸν Ἑρμῆν· ὁ δὲ λόγος, ἄϋπνον ἐπιστάμενος φύσιν τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ, διδασκέτω ἡμᾶς ὅτι κατὰ καιροὺς οἰκονομεῖ τὰ τοῦ κόσμου πράγματα ὁ θεὸς, ὡς ἀπαιτεῖ τὸ εὔλογον. οὐ θαυμαστὸν δὲ εἰ διὰ τὸ μεγάλας εἶναι καὶ δυσδιηγήτους τὰς κρίσεις τοῦ θεοῦ αἱ „ἀπαίδευτοι“ πλανῶνται „ψυχαὶ,“ καὶ Κέλσος σὺν αὐταῖς. οὐδὲν οὖν καταγέλαστόν ἐστιν ἐν τῷ Ἰουδαίοις, παρ᾿ οἷς γεγόνασιν οἱ προφῆται, πεπέμφθαι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ· ἵν᾿ ἐκεῖθεν ἀρξάμενος σωματικῶς δυνάμει καὶ πνεύματι ἀνατείλῃ τῇ μηκέτι βουλομένῃ ἐρήμῳ θεοῦ τυγχάνειν οἰκουμένῃ ψυχῶν.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore there was no need (χρεία) for many bodies to come to be everywhere and many spirits analogous (ἀνάλογον) to Jesus, so that the whole inhabited world of humans be enlightened (φωτισθῇ) by the Word of God. For the one Word sufficed (ἤρκει), having risen (ἀνατείλας) as 'sun of righteousness', to send out from Judea the rays (αὐγάς) reaching to the soul of those wishing to receive him. If someone longs (ποθεῖ) to see many bodies filled with divine spirit, ministering (διακονούμενα) analogously to that one Christ to the salvation (σωτηρία) of humans everywhere, let him consider those who everywhere teach soundly (ὑγιῶς) and with upright life (βίου ὀρθοῦ) the word of Jesus, themselves also called Christs (Χριστοί) by the divine Scriptures in 'Do not touch my Christs, and among my prophets do no evil (πονηρεύεσθε).' For as we heard 'that antichrist comes', and no less learned that 'many antichrists' are in the world, in the same way knowing that Christ has sojourned (ἐπιδεδήμηκε) we observe that through him many Christs have come to be in the world, who analogously to him loved 'righteousness and' hated 'injustice (ἀδικία); and therefore anointed (ἔχρισε)' them also 'God, the God' of Christ, 'with oil of gladness (ἐλαίῳ ἀγαλλιάσεως)'. But he, above (ὑπέρ) his 'sharers/fellows (μετόχους)', having loved 'righteousness and' hated 'lawlessness (ἀνομία)', took both the firstfruits (ἀπαρχή) of the anointing (χρῖσμα) and, if one must so name it, the whole anointing of the oil of 'gladness'; his sharers, each as he had room (κεχώρηκε), shared (μετέσχον) also in his anointing. Therefore, since Christ is 'head of the church', so that Christ and the church are one body, the 'ointment (μύρον) upon the head' has come down 'upon the beard (πώγωνα)', the symbols (σύμβολα) of the perfect/full-grown man (τελείου ἀνδρός), 'Aaron', and this 'ointment coming down' reached 'upon the hem (ὤαν) of his garment'. These things are said by me against the unseemly (ἄσεμνον) word of Celsus who said: 'It was necessary to breathe alike many bodies and send them over the whole inhabited world.' The comic poet, making laughter, made Zeus sleeping and being woken and sending Hermes to the Greeks; but the word/doctrine (λόγος), knowing the nature of God as sleepless (ἄϋπνον), let it teach us that according to seasons (κατὰ καιρούς) God manages (οἰκονομεῖ) the affairs of the world, as the reasonable (τὸ εὔλογον) demands. Not wonderful if, through God's judgments (κρίσεις) being great and hard to narrate (δυσδιηγήτους), the 'uninstructed (ἀπαίδευτοι) souls' wander (πλανῶνται), and Celsus with them. Nothing then laughable in the Son of God having been sent to Jews, among whom the prophets came to be, so that beginning from there bodily (σωματικῶς) with power and spirit he might rise (ἀνατείλῃ) on the inhabited world of souls no longer wishing to be desolate (ἐρήμῳ) of God.
pass_b_english: That is why there was no need for many bodies to come into being everywhere, with many spirits like that of Jesus, in order that the whole inhabited world of men might be enlightened by the Word of God. The one Word was enough, rising as the “sun of righteousness” (Malachi 4:2), to send out from Judea the rays that reach the souls of those willing to receive him. And if anyone longs to see many bodies filled with a divine spirit, serving, as that one Christ did, the salvation of men everywhere, let him consider those who everywhere teach the word of Jesus soundly and with an upright life. The divine Scriptures call them christs too, in the verse: “Do not touch my christs, and do my prophets no harm” (Psalm 105:15). For just as we have heard “that antichrist is coming,” and have learned no less that there are “many antichrists” in the world (1 John 2:18), in the same way, knowing that Christ has come, we see that because of him many christs have come into being in the world. Like him, they have “loved righteousness and hated injustice; and therefore God, the God” of Christ, “has anointed” them too “with the oil of gladness” (Psalm 45:7; Hebrews 1:9). But he, who loved “righteousness” and hated “lawlessness” more than his “companions” (Psalm 45:7), received the firstfruits of the anointing and, if one may so name it, the whole anointing with the oil of “gladness”; while his companions, each according to his capacity, shared in his anointing too. Therefore, since Christ is “the head of the church” (Ephesians 5:23), so that Christ and the church are one body, “the ointment upon the head” has come down “upon the beard,” the marks of the full-grown man, the beard “of Aaron”; and this “ointment,” “coming down,” has reached “to the hem of his garment” (Psalm 133:2).

This too I have said in answer to the unseemly argument of Celsus, when he said: “He ought to have breathed it alike into many bodies and sent them out over the whole world.” The comic poet, then, to raise a laugh, made Zeus sleep, wake up, and send Hermes to the Greeks. But let our doctrine, which knows that God’s nature never sleeps, teach us that God orders the affairs of the world at fitting times, as reason requires. And it is no wonder if, because the judgments of God are great and hard to set forth, “uninstructed souls” go astray (Wisdom of Solomon 17:1), and Celsus with them. There is nothing laughable, then, in the fact that the Son of God was sent to the Jews, among whom the prophets had arisen, so that, beginning there in the body, he might rise with power and spirit upon the world of souls, which no longer wished to be left empty of God.

choices.choice: LXX renumbering: ‘sun of righteousness’ is LXX Malachi 3:20 = English Malachi 4:2; ‘Do not touch my christs’ is LXX Psalm 104:15 = English Psalm 105:15 (the same words stand at 1 Chronicles 16:22); ‘loved righteousness... oil of gladness... companions’ is LXX Psalm 44:8 = English Psalm 45:7, also quoted at Hebrews 1:9; ‘ointment upon the head... hem of his garment’ is LXX Psalm 132:2 = English Psalm 133:2. Origen quotes the psalm first with ἀδικίαν (‘injustice’) and then with ἀνομίαν (‘lawlessness’, the LXX reading); both kept. In ‘God, the God of Christ’ Origen keeps ‘God, the God’ from the psalm and puts ‘of Christ’ in place of ‘your’; the quotation marks follow that split. His ὑπὲρ τοὺς μετόχους stands for LXX παρὰ τοὺς μετόχους; ‘more than his companions’ keeps the sense. μέτοχοι (‘sharers’) and μετέσχον (‘shared’) are a play on words that English ‘companions... shared’ only partly keeps. Χριστοί is rendered ‘christs’ (lowercase: anointed men, not God) so that Origen’s argument from the word stays visible. ‘The marks of the full-grown man’ (τὰ σύμβολα τοῦ τελείου ἀνδρός) may echo Ephesians 4:13 (‘to a mature man’); possible allusion, not cited inline. ‘A divine spirit’ (θείου πνεύματος) is left lowercase because Origen is answering Celsus’s phrase about many spirits; it may mean the Holy Spirit. ὁ λόγος in ‘let our doctrine... teach us’ is ambiguous (our teaching, reason, or the divine Word); ‘our doctrine’ is chosen for the contrast with the comic poet, and ‘our’ is implied, not stated. ‘God’s nature never sleeps’ may recall Psalm 121:4 (LXX 120:4); possible allusion, not cited. ‘Head of the church’ matches Ephesians 5:23 word for word (compare Colossians 1:18; Ephesians 1:22-23 for the one body). Wisdom 17:1 reads ‘For great are your judgments and hard to set forth; therefore uninstructed souls went astray’: Origen’s ‘great and hard to set forth’ is part of the same allusion.
